spots.n: Pike Place Market & the Gum Wall
spots.s: The market gauntlet — flying fish, flower stalls and the gloriously gross Gum Wall in Post Alley; Seattle's default great first date.
The 605-ft icon with tilting glass benches and a rotating glass floor — pricey, but worth it once.
Glass fever dream at the Needle's feet — the garden glows at golden hour; date catnip.
The postcard: skyline, Elliott Bay and Rainier from a pocket-size Queen Anne overlook.
Boats rise, salmon climb — hit the fish-ladder viewing windows July–Sept, then stroll the botanical garden; free.
Rusting refinery turned kite hill — THE sunset-over-the-skyline spot across Lake Union.
500 acres of bluff and forest ending at a working lighthouse — the loop trail is the city's best walk-and-talk.
The VW-crushing troll under the Aurora Bridge — five silly minutes that make any date itinerary.
West Seattle's beach strip — skyline views across the bay, volleyball and summer bonfire smoke.
Gehry's purple blob of pop culture — Hendrix, horror props and indie-game arcades.
Downtown's serious art anchor under the Hammering Man — free first Thursdays.
THE cheap date: 35 minutes across the Sound on foot from Colman Dock, wine bars in Winslow, skyline both ways.
Sunset beach with fire pits and Olympic-range views — claim a pit early on summer Saturdays.
230 acres of UW gardens along Lake Washington — Azalea Way in spring is absurd.
1912 glass palm house atop Capitol Hill — pair it with the water-tower viewpoint; cheap and lovely.
Ride the 1914 elevators to a speakeasy-style observatory bar — the smarter, boozier Needle alternative.
Gondolas over Elliott Bay on Pier 57 — touristy, sure, but golden hour up there works.
20 hidden acres of Japanese-American garden artistry in Rainier Beach — waterfalls, moon bridges, zero crowds.
SAM's free sculptures rolling down to the Sound — Calder against the Olympics at sunset.
Wisecracking walk through the buried 1889 storefronts under Pioneer Square — a reliable icebreaker.
Concorde, SR-71 and a walk-through 747 at Boeing Field — the aviation-nerd afternoon that never misses.

nightlife.s: Three rooms of hip-hop, Top 40 and Latin under Pioneer Square brick — Seattle's longest-running big-club night out.
Capitol Hill's big-room floor on a Funktion-One rig — rotating hip-hop, house and EDM nights.
SoDo loft with a rooftop deck — sunset day parties and house sets above the train tracks.
Glittery SoDo disco-warehouse — inclusive crowd, go-go stages, house and hip-hop till late.
Fremont's covered-patio live room — a steady diet of hip-hop, funk and reggae bookings.
Pike/Pine's anchor venue — touring rap and R&B upstairs, DJs and club nights at Barboza in the basement.
The grunge-era legend reborn in Belltown — multiple stages, comedy and late-night hangs.
1939 ballroom steps from Pike Place — the city's best mid-size stage before a downtown nightcap.
Scrappy Madison club mixing rap showcases, dance nights and indie bills.
Beacon Hill's party room — hip-hop and dance nights with pizza slices to soak it up.
White-tablecloth jazz institution since 1979 — dinner-and-a-legend date night downtown.
Plush supper club beneath Wild Ginger — R&B, soul and world acts with cocktails at a booth.
Columbia City's musician-run room — jazz, soul and genre-hopping bills most nights, cheap cover.
A whiskey library of world renown — thousands of bottles and impeccable cocktails for a slow conversation.
Belltown speakeasy down a boiler-room alley — quiet, candlelit, made for a second date.
Rooftop above Pike Place — Elliott Bay sunsets, sharp cocktails and ferry lights for the closer.
Japanese-style private-room karaoke on Capitol Hill — book a room, split some sake, sing badly together.

eats.s: Belltown Edomae temple founded by Shiro Kashiba — sit at the bar and order omakase, period.
Shiro-san's Pike Place room and the city's marquee sushi counter — book a month out for the full omakase.
Ten-seat kaiseki-omakase hidden in a Broadway alley — two dozen exquisite courses; reservations drop monthly.
Ravenna's Edomae sleeper — Tsukiji-trained precision at two-thirds the downtown tab.
Wallingford's beloved no-frills sushi counter — the value play locals happily line up for.
Belltown sushi house with a giant sake list — the late-night happy hour outclasses most full-price menus.
Japantown's 120-year-old izakaya — tatami rooms, black cod collar, pure old-Seattle soul.
Handmade soba and duck from a James Beard-recognized Fremont gem — date-night noodles, elevated.
Serious Tokyo-style ramen born in Japan, grown here — the Capitol Hill shop nails smoky shoyu.
Effervescent Pike/Pine izakaya — small plates, sake flights and a loud, happy bar.
The family that brought pho to Seattle, now in a neon corner shop — brisket bowls and stiff cocktails.
Street-food canteen by Seattle U — rotisserie, vermicelli bowls and strong espresso martinis.
Tiny Lao powerhouse on Madison — laab, sticky rice and chili heat worth the squeeze.
Crossroads-area KBBQ standby — charcoal tables and a proper banchan spread a block from 99 Ranch.
Ballard's jewel-box oyster bar — split a dozen and a glass of Muscadet at the zinc counter.
Filipinx soul food on Beacon Hill — communal, generous and one of the city's warmest rooms.

chinese.s: Old-school Chengdu kitchen on the Eastside — mapo tofu and twice-cooked pork with a real huajiao buzz.
Bellevue Sichuan veterans who cooked in-province for decades — water-boiled fish and dry-fried green beans that taste of home.
The ID's quintessential cart-style dim sum — go early on weekends for har gow and egg tarts.
Hong Kong-style cafe open past 1a — dim sum by day, congee and neon by night.
Cash-friendly wonton-and-congee counter — the ID's best quick solo lunch.
The Bellevue-born xiao long bao chain at its Chinatown-ID outpost — soup dumplings and q-bao without the DTF wait.
The Taipei dumpling empire's first Northwest room at Lincoln Square — precision xiao long bao, every time.
The Sichuan hot-pot giant in downtown Bellevue — table-side noodle dancing and full-service spectacle.
Hand-ripped biang-biang noodles and cumin lamb by UW — Xi'an street food done right.
Taiwanese family kitchen famous for the pork pancake burger — worth the Bellevue line since 2006.
The 1928-founded pan-Asian superstore anchoring the ID — groceries, food court and Kinokuniya books in one stop.
Crossroads' Chinese-market mothership — live tanks, roast duck and every pantry staple.
Pike Place hum bao window since 1979 — BBQ pork buns to fuel the market stroll.
Smithsonian-affiliated museum of the Asian Pacific American story — book the historic hotel tour.

chinese.n: Hing Hay Park 慶喜公園 & Chinatown Gate
chinese.s: The ID's living-room plaza — grand pavilion, ping-pong tables and the historic China gate a block away.
Sichuan-style courtyard garden above the city in West Seattle — a quiet corner of Chengdu with skyline views.
The ID's biggest day — lion dances, Hing Hay Park stage and a 40+ stop food walk; watch CIDBIA for the late-winter date.
One September night of lanterns, food stalls and lion dances on King St — Mid-Autumn energy at full blast.

fishing.s: THE in-city salmon pier — winter blackmouth, Aug–Sep coho and pinks, squid jigging on fall nights; WA saltwater license + free catch record card required.
WDFW's year-round pier north of town — salmon runs, crab in season and winter squid under the lights.
Six-pack charter trolling Puget Sound kings and coho out of Shilshole, minutes from Ballard — license and catch card on you.
40-year Seattle charter outfit chasing salmon and lingcod from Shilshole Bay Marina — gear and coaching included.
Stocked rainbows a jog from downtown — bank and dock fishing year-round with a WA freshwater license.
Smallmouth, jumbo perch and fall coho in the city's backyard lake — launch or bank-fish at Stan Sayres.
Wade the West Seattle gravel for sea-run cutthroat, plus odd-year pinks off the beach; saltwater license applies.
Summer trout water 40 minutes out — swing the Fall City reaches below the falls (freshwater license).
Legendary Sky steelhead and salmon bar water near Gold Bar — check WDFW emergency rules before every trip; catch record card mandatory.

WDFW's pick for wild coastal cutthroat, smallmouth and yellow perch on the 4,800-acre lake — launch at the state park (Discover Pass plus a launch fee); kokanee and steelhead are closed and salmon opens only in good years.
A WDFW-listed public pier south of the city with lights, railings and a fish-cleaning station, rated good for squid jigging on dark evenings — the parking lot closes 10p–5a.

biking.s: Evergreen's flow-and-jump mecca in the Issaquah Alps — pro-built lines from mellow Boot Camp XC to the Voodoo Child jump line.
Big-mountain XC and enduro from the Tiger Summit trailhead — earn 1,800 ft and rip Predator and Off the Grid back down.
The newer DNR network next door to Tiger — Flow State's miles-long descent is worth the whole drive.
12 miles of rooty, rolling singletrack linking Issaquah toward Duthie — the classic lunch-loop dirt.
Techy all-weather skills park under the freeway deck — Seattle's rainy-day dirt fix, minutes from downtown.
Punchy forested loops above Lake Washington on old seminary grounds — bring a Discover Pass.
13 miles of buff beginner-to-intermediate singletrack in the Maltby woods — a great confidence-builder.
The 27-mile paved classic — spin from Ballard's breweries along the ship canal to Lake Washington, car-free.
Black Diamond's 15-mile web of tight, twisty singletrack with ladder bridges, drops and other freeride features — no long climbs, just a few rooty steep pitches around sharp corners.
About 15 miles of very well maintained single- and double-track on a hilltop southeast of Monroe — mostly flat on top, with a big drop if you ride down to the Snohomish River.

social.s: The Capitol Hill ballroom's Thursday institution — 9p intro lesson, then a packed, friendly floor till 1a; no partner needed.
All-vinyl salsa on the sprung ballroom floor — old-school mambo energy, beginners genuinely welcome.
Fremont studio's weekly blowout — three rooms of salsa, bachata and zouk after drop-in classes; walk-ins welcome.
Free 6:29a bootcamp with hugs and high-fives — Gas Works in summer, Seattle Center in winter; just show up.

social.n: Green Lake Running Group Evening Run
social.s: Decades-old drop-in run around the lake — 3/5/7-mile options and a chatty pace group for every level.
The Tuesday-night jam running since '97 in a Pioneer Square Irish pub — free, late and full of players.

social.n: Ballard Board Game Night at Mox Boarding House
social.s: Free weekly meetup at Ballard's board-game palace — a new game every 45 minutes and an instant table of strangers.

social.n: Geeks Who Drink Trivia at the Unicorn
social.s: Free seven-round pub quiz in the carnival-themed Capitol Hill bar — join a short team and make friends fast.
Year-round Sunday flea — vintage stalls, food trucks and canal-side people-watching.
The city's best year-round farmers market takes over brick-lined Ballard Ave every Sunday.
Mandarin study-and-chat meetup — low-pressure Chinese practice with fellow learners at ID cafes; locations rotate.

social.n: FREE Drop-in Social Foam Dodgeball @ Montlake Community Center
social.s: Come play fun, social, good-vibes dodgeball! When enough people show up will start playing games. Come have lots of fun with friendly people in a social, inclusive setting. Tuesdays from 6p with Eastside Foam Dodgeball and Offbeat Fun at Montlake Community Center, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Pickleball for Beginners at Green Lake (Thursday Afternoons)
social.s: Returning players should place orange cones on the courts, to take a maximum of 4 of the 8 courts. Thursdays from 11a with Seattle Beginner Pickleball at Green Lake Tennis and Pickleball Courts East, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

Join us for a run Saturday morning! We will then make our way to the Elliot Bay Trail for our run. We have a 3mi and 6mi route options posted below. Option 1: 3mi route, run north to Alaskan Way N and back. Saturdays from 8a with Elliott Bay Running Club at Meet at Broad St & Elliott Ave, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Discovery Park hike, Serendipity cafe, and Ballard's farmer market
social.s: We will hike the loop plus the North and South beach for a total of about 5 miles with several opportunities to cut short. Picture is for a general idea of the route only. Sundays from 7:30a with Washington Weekends at Discovery park North parking lot, seattle · no Meetup fee.
We'll play small-sided games on small goals. Sundays from 11a with Seattle Soccer Pickup at Seattle University Park · no Meetup fee.

Play as easy or hard as you like. Leave when you want but we all end by 8. The goal of the game is to have a good time! Two teams, soft polo ball, pass it around, toss it around until you hit something. Wednesdays from 5:15p with Kirkland Kayak Polo at Marsh Park, Kirkland · $1 on Meetup.

All intermediate-to-advanced volleyball players are invited to join us every Tuesday when school is in session for recreational level play. Tuesdays from 6:30p with The Puget Sound Volleyball Meetup Group at Hazel Valley Elementary School, Burien · $5 on Meetup.
We'll play small-sided games on small goals. Saturdays from 9a with Seattle Pickup Soccer Club at Cal Anderson Park, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

social.n: SeattleU Park CoEd Pick Up Soccer
social.s: We'll play small-sided games on small goals. Sundays from 2p with Seattle Soccer Pickup at Seattle University Park · no Meetup fee.
Join for one, join for both. Tuesdays from 5:30a with Sweaty Betties at Green Lake Community Center, Seattle · no Meetup fee.
Mondays from 7p with Free Pickup Dodgeball in Ballard at Loyal Heights Community Center, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

Join us for a pleasant evening of fishing for a variety of Pan Fish including Bass, Perch, Trout and even the occasional Catfish will show up from time to time. Tuesdays from 6p with Angling Northwest Fishing & Fly Fishing. at David E Brink Park, Kirkland · no Meetup fee.
Wednesdays from 7a with Liveable Kirkland at Kirkland Rotary Central Station · no Meetup fee.

Beginner Lindy Hop 1 Dance Class with Swing It Seattle Tuesdays 11/17-12/15 7:15-8:05 Russian Community Center 704 19th Ave E, Seattle Free Parking Discover the joyous fun of the original swing dance, Lindy… Tuesdays from 7:15p with Seattle Anti-Freeze at Russian Community Center, Seattle · $109 on Meetup.

social.n: Swing Dance Classes with Katie & Mark Kihara of Swing It Seattle
social.s: Beginner Lindy Hop 1 Class Mondays 11/16-12/14 (5 weeks) 6:15-7:05 South Park Hall 1253 S Cloverdale St, Seattle, WA 98108 Free Parking Discover the joyous fun of the original swing dance, Lindy Hop! Mondays from 6:15p with Seattle Dance Meetup at South Park Hall, Seattle · $109 on Meetup.

Join the Visually Speaking signing squad at the Pub for Weekly Voices Off Meetups at Hopvine Pub! Every Monday from 4- 8 pm, The Hopvine Pub transforms into a designated space for ASL immersion. Mondays from 4p with Capitol Hill ASL Meet Up at Hopvine Pub, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Learn to Swing Dance (¡ ᗯᗩᑎTEᗪ TO ᗪO TᕼᗩT . . . ᒍᑌᔕT ᑎOT ᗩᒪOᑎE ! ! ! ℠ Seattle)
social.s: Beginner Lindy Hop 1 Dance Class with Swing It Seattle Mondays 11/16-12/14 (5 weeks) 6:15-7:05 South Park Hall 1253 S Cloverdale St, Seattle, WA 98108 Free Parking Discover the joyous fun of the original… Mondays from 6:15p with ¡ ᗯᗩᑎTEᗪ TO ᗪO TᕼᗩT . . . ᒍᑌᔕT ᑎOT ᗩᒪOᑎE ! ! ! ℠ Seattle at South Park Hall, Seattle · $109 on Meetup.

social.n: Swing It Wednesday - Live Swing Music & Dance at South Park Hall
social.s: Join us at the new home of Swing It Wednesday! South Park Hall (est 1926) is a spectacular venue that was built for live music & dance. Wednesdays from 8:15p with Seattle Dance Meetup at South Park Hall, Seattle · $18 on Meetup.

Whether you're a new or experienced board gamer, you can join us for an evening of board games and socializing at the Lincoln Square South Food Hall! Fridays from 7p with The Millennial Social Club at Lincoln South Food Hall, Bellevue · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Board Game Night Coffee & Tea Social in the U-District UW Seattle
social.s: Join our board game night—for an engaging game night at the Hilton! Fridays from 6:30p with U-District Board Games Social at Graduate Hotel lobby, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

Our Sunday weekly meetups are in Seattle at Stoup Brewing on Capitol Hill! This meetup is for players of any skill level, be it first-time players or seasoned veterans. Sundays from 12p with Seattle Riichi Mahjong Club at Stoup Brewing - Capitol Hill, Seattle · no Meetup fee.
Come join us for board games at TeKu Tavern. Open to all experience levels. Feel free to bring your own games. Sundays from 2p with Puget Sound Board Games at TeKu Tavern, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Thursday Board Games at Shoreline UUC!
social.s: A weekly event held at the Shoreline Unitarian Universalist Church. We typically play strategy board games from light-moderate complexity to moderate complexity, typically until 8-10 pm. Thursdays from 6p with Seattle Board Games at Shoreline UU Church, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

remote.s: In the historic Guiry and Schillestad Building at 92 Lenora St, a block north of Pike Place Market. Drop-ins are M–F 9a–5p: hot desks and standing bars, gigabit Wi-Fi, phone booths, plus coffee, tea and sparkling water. Members also get conference-room hours (2–4 a month) and 6a–6p or 24/7 access; prepaying saves 20%. Sister spaces in Ballard and West Canal Yards.
remote.b: Soft music and a low murmur of conversation; booths for private calls

remote.s: WeWork in the historic Holyoke Building at 1st & Spring, near the Seattle Art Museum and a short walk south of Pike Place. Book a day pass in the WeWork app for a hot desk in the shared lounge. All Access also covers 1201 3rd Ave (day pass from $49), Hawk Tower, Ballard's NW Market St and Bellevue. Monthly prices are often on promo.
remote.p: Day pass from $39 · All Access from $187/mo
remote.b: Phone booths and meeting rooms usually available, per reviews

remote.s: In the Kelly Springfield Building at 1525 11th Ave, between Pike and Pine. Day passes cover shared tables and common areas on weekdays 9a–4p: outlets, fast Wi-Fi, free coffee & tea, phone booths, kitchens, printers and a rooftop patio. Coworking members get $10/mo in printing credits and 20% off rooms, and can add 24/7 access for $100/mo.
remote.p: $40 day pass · coworking from $95/mo · dedicated desk $500/mo

remote.s: In the historic Lake Union Building at 1700 Westlake Ave N, right on the water. Gigabit internet, phone booths, a free huddle room for calls, unlimited coffee & tea, bike racks, showers and lockers. Members can borrow stand-up paddleboards, and there's a floating workspace. Startup experts in residence and 24/7 app access for members. Meeting rooms from $25/hr.
remote.b: Very quiet; one visitor counted three other people outside the private offices

remote.s: 3rd floor of 400 University St at Rainier Square, in the downtown core. Unlimited craft coffee and snacks, privacy booths, a kitchen, bike storage, outdoor space, pet friendly. The polished, hotel-style option for a full day of calls. M–F 9a–5p.

Rem Koolhaas's 11-floor glass library at 1000 4th Ave, home of the Books Spiral. Free Wi-Fi, seating and tables with outlets, public computers and in-library laptops, a coffee cart and underground paid parking for about 143 cars. The Central Library's meeting rooms are paid, but branch study rooms are free. Mon & Fri–Sun 10–6, Tue–Thu 10–8.
remote.b: Weekends busier; weekdays plenty of seats with outlets

remote.s: Branch at 5614 22nd Ave NW in central Ballard. Free study rooms (like every SPL branch room), a quiet room, Wi-Fi, print/copy/scan and fax, bike racks and free parking. Air-conditioned, which matters in a Seattle August. Mon & Fri–Sun 10–6, Tue–Thu 10–8.
remote.b: Mostly quiet crowd; glass-walled quiet room and silent study rooms

remote.s: Minimal, sun-flooded café at 524 1st Ave S in Pioneer Square, open weekdays only. The Infatuation calls it a Pioneer Square landmark for remote work. A short walk from the stadiums and King Street Station.
remote.b: Main floor bustles; upstairs seating is the quieter spot

remote.s: Caffè Vita's counter in KEXP's gathering space on 1st Ave N, next to Seattle Center and the Space Needle. You work while watching the station's live on-air shows, recorded a few feet away in a sound booth, and there's a vinyl kiosk in the back. The Infatuation tags it for getting work done.
remote.b: Busy on weekends and seating is limited; music can be loud

remote.s: Coffee bar at 665 S King St in the Chinatown-International District, opened in 2025 a short walk from King Street Station. The Infatuation calls it a treasure for general laptop work, with reliable Wi-Fi, and tags it for being left alone. Pastries and sandwiches, toffee miso lattes and ceremonial matcha.
remote.b: Limited seating, so arrive early; relaxed for long stays

events.s: Giant illuminated animal lanterns along the zoo's paths, 4–9p nightly with last entry 8:30p. It's closed some nights (11/16–18, 11/23, 11/26, 11/30, 12/7, 12/14, 12/24–25 and several in January), so check before you go.
The Cascadia rivalry at Climate Pledge Arena: Seattle hosts Vancouver. Doors at 5:10p.

events.n: Pacific Northwest Ballet: George Balanchine's The Nutcracker
events.s: PNB's Balanchine Nutcracker with Ian Falconer's sets, at McCaw Hall. Look for themed shows: Beer & Ballet Night (12/16), Ugly Sweater Day (12/18) and Pajama Day (12/27).
Monday Night Football at Lumen Field.
An early-afternoon December home game at Lumen Field.

events.n: Victoria Monét: Frequency of Love Tour
events.s: The Grammy-winning R&B singer plays WaMu Theater next to Lumen Field. The floor is standing room.
The touring Broadway revival plays the Paramount over the holidays. Captioned, ASL-interpreted and sensory-friendly performances are scheduled.
Christmas night football at Lumen Field against NFC West rival LA.
The comedian and author does a stand-up set at the Neptune Theatre in the U District. Reserved seating; doors 6p, show 7p. Buying at the Paramount box office cuts the fees.
The bassist and funk-soul singer brings his Distracted AF tour to Showbox SoDo, with fera opening. Doors 7p, show 8p; cashless venue.
A German-style holiday market at Seattle Center with timed-entry tickets. Weekdays 4–9p and weekends 11:30a–9p until Dec 13, longer hours in the final week. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day.

The Downtown Seattle Association lights the holiday tree and star in Westlake Park on the day after Thanksgiving, with afternoon activities from 11a. The holiday carousel opens the same day and runs through Jan 3.

Bellevue Botanical Garden's walk-through holiday light display; timed half-hour entry, tickets online in advance. Entry 4:30–9p; $10 (ages 11+), $5 on select early-December nights, kids free. Closed Dec 25.

Snoop plays a live set and a DJ set at Angel of the Winds Arena in Everett, with Waka Flocka, Baby Bash and Travis Porter. The night is billed for West Coast classics and throwback hip-hop. Doors 6p, show 7:30p.
Saturday from 6p with The Seattle Thaw - Making New Friends Despite The Freeze at ChefShop, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

events.n: [Capitol Hill] Japanese Conversation Meetup at Katsu Burger
events.s: Come take part and meet others interested in learning Japanese (or English) like you! Monday from 6p with Seattle Peer Japanese Study at Katsu Burger Capitol Hill, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Trivia Night at Gearhouse Coffee Shop
events.s: Gearhouse is all about making new friends and getting people outside, so come with a team or solo and we'll help you find a team! Monday from 6:30p with Gearhouse Community Events at Gearhouse, Seattle · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Escape Room MeetUp! Escape Room Board Games @ Lincoln Food Hall - Bellevue!
events.s: Come by, say hi, grab some grub, and play escape room and possibly generic board games in this social event! We’ll have some escape games. Feel free to bring your own puzzles and games too! Tuesday from 6p with Seattle Escape Room Meetup at Lincoln South Food Hall, Bellevue · no Meetup fee.

We're back with another board game meetup. Come hang out for a fun Friday evening of board games, card games, and a chance to meet and connect with other Malayalis in the Seattle area. Friday from 6:30p with Malayalam Conversation Meetup (Kerala/Malayalee) at Mox Boarding House, Seattle · no Meetup fee.
Tacoma's long-running holiday light show strings the zoo grounds with displays of animals and sea life. Timed tickets are sold online, and the zoo is closed Dec 24–25.
A free nightly 7p parade of drummers, dancers and falling snow along Bellevue Way between Bellevue Square and Lincoln Square.
Choir-carrying sailings tour the Sound and Lake Union, stopping at shoreline parks for carols, with a Parade of Boats on 12/11 and a Lake Union finale on 12/23. Opening night departs Pier 55.
Washington closes its Husky Stadium season against Indiana, the defending national champions, with the lake behind the open end zone.
Washington visits Climate Pledge Arena in what may be Alexander Ovechkin's final trip to Seattle.
The jazz-meets-R&B-and-hip-hop pianist plays an early 6p and a late 9:30p set at Fremont's Nectar Lounge, 21+.
The deadpan Southern stand-up brings his front-porch storytelling to the historic Moore Theatre.

iceskating.s: The Kraken's three-rink complex at Northgate runs public skate at lunch, in the evenings and on weekends. It costs $16.29 + tax, rentals are $6.33 + tax, and you book through Dash. On select game days, Skate & Watch shows the Kraken broadcast on rink 1's big screen during public skate, next on Nov 12 and 14.

A 9,000+ sq ft real-ice rink in Bellevue Downtown Park, a block south of Bellevue Square, open Nov 13, 2026 to Jan 18, 2027. Admission includes skates and buys 75 minutes on the ice. One price covers all ages, and weekdays cost less than weekends. A tent covers the ice, so it runs rain or shine, but high winds can close it.

Kent's year-round rink charges $18.18 general admission (3 and under free), plus $6 skates and $3 helmets. Black Light skates run Friday and Saturday nights in 75-minute sessions, with extra nights over the holiday break. There's 18-hole mini golf and batting cages on site. Booking online is recommended, though walk-ins are welcome.

A nonprofit rink in Lynnwood that bills itself as the Northwest's premier public-skating facility. Public sessions follow a daily schedule posted online, with hockey and figure-skate rentals. It also runs stick-and-puck, learn-to-skate classes and even theatre on ice. There's a warm lobby and a snack bar for anyone sitting out.

Mountlake Terrace's rink on 70th Ave W, a short hop up I-5 past Shoreline. Public-skate times are posted on its site only as a schedule image, so check before heading up. The arena also runs lunch-hour hockey and figure-skating ice, and its pro shop is open seven days a week.

Sno-King's Kirkland rink in Kingsgate is the home office of a three-rink group that also runs Renton and Snoqualmie. All three list public skate sessions, booked through the DaySmart system, and a drop-in calendar covers the rest of the open ice. Check the Sno-King site for each rink's current public-skate times before driving over.

skating.s: A 2.8-mile paved loop that is one of Seattle's busiest car-free trails. Skaters and bikes take the outer lane, one way in the direction of the arrows, at 10 mph max, and walkers keep to the lake side. The park draws thousands a day, so go early on sunny weekends. Motorized boards and scooters are banned.

The region's best-known rail-trail runs 20 miles from Shilshole Bay to Bothell. It's paved the whole way except an on-road gap in Ballard, and King County names skaters among its regulars. It passes Fremont, Gas Works Park, UW and Matthews Beach. Weekday rush brings bike commuters, so midday and weekends skate easier.

West Seattle's widened beachfront path along Alki Beach Park, about 2.5 miles from Duwamish Head to Alki Point on Elliott Bay, with downtown skyline views. Seattle Parks says summer brings joggers, rollerbladers and cyclists, so mornings are calmer. Parking lines Alki Ave SW, and restrooms are at the Alki Point end.

The closest skate route to Pike Place: the waterfront trail through Myrtle Edwards Park, just north of the Olympic Sculpture Park. Seattle Parks renovated and repaved the bike trail, adding lighting, bike racks and repair stations, with separate pedestrian paths alongside. It's flat with Elliott Bay views, and the W Thomas St overpass connects it to Uptown.

A flat, car-free 2.4-mile loop around the Bailey Peninsula on Lake Washington, repaved in 2007 and used by walkers, runners, cyclists and rollerbladers. It has views of Mount Rainier and Mercer Island on one side and old-growth forest on the other. It's a shorter, quieter alternative to Green Lake.

10.1 miles paved along the Sammamish River from Bothell to Marymoor Park in Redmond, with a soft shoulder and views of the valley, the Cascade foothills and Rainier. King County lists skaters among its users, and it joins the Burke-Gilman in Bothell. Horses share the corridor between Woodinville and Marymoor.

Follows a historic rail line up the Cedar River from Lake Washington in Renton. The first 12.3 miles are paved, and the last five toward Landsburg are soft-surface. A section near the Dorre Don Natural Area has been closed since the winter 2025 floods, so skate out from Renton and check the county notice before heading far upriver.

White Center's roller rink runs 21+ nights all week, 8:30–11p: Tuesday R&B and hip-hop with DJ Slayground, Saturday's Sk8 Party (old school, funk, hip-hop, $18) and Sunday's Roll Around Seatown (hip-hop, R&B, soul).
